chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v01] Now the rite described by Shiva is set forth for attaining disciplehood: when a teacher wishes to appoint one established in the vow into disciplehood, guruhood, or adept-hood.

[tal-a16-v10] Ganapati, guru, Parama, Paramesthi, and the prior-siddha speech-field-lord, thus seven are named in the guru-row rite to be fully worshipped by our gurus.

[tal-a16-v02] After performing consecration, on the second day one should draw the mandala in the collective rite and elsewhere as stated.

[tal-a16-v03] By the count of six, eight, and double twenty-four, the five-wheel system is called in the scripture named Shri-prior.

[tal-a16-v04] Thirty-two and its double, in the Shri-mat-Traishira view, and the connection with countless wheels, are described in the Shri-Siddha beginning.

[tal-a16-v05] Therefore, as the sacrifice is measured by the wheel, one should worship accordingly; by that, here one should draw three tridents.

[tal-a16-v06] In the three tridents, the three goddesses, by rotational course and by middle-left-right distinction, should become fully worshipped.

[tal-a16-v07] Maintenance before the mandala will be taught briefly: having drawn the mandala, one wipes it with scented cloth.

[tal-a16-v08] Having bathed, the guru, before the mandala here, should worship the external deities and the door deities at the door place.

[tal-a16-v09] In the front part of the mandala, from the northeast direction in order up to the southeast, one should fully worship Ganesha and the others up to the field protectors.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v11] Then, having taken command, the support power and related deities, worshipped with flowers, incense, and so forth, are sufficient from the trident root onward.

[tal-a16-v12] Up to Shiva, at the end of the white lotus, among the three tridents in order, true being should be in the middle trident together with the supreme.

[tal-a16-v13] On the left, together with another, the nine-souled one is right-going and supreme; on the trident's right, standing on the middle peak, is Rati-crown.

[tal-a16-v14] May it be together with supreme and lower powers: on the right Bhairava abides supremely, on the left on the trident, standing in the middle, the nine-souled one with another.

[tal-a16-v15] May it be supreme, together with the supreme power, on the left side, and Bhairava; thus, when Shri Para Devi is established in the all-pervading state.

[tal-a16-v16] The sacrifice becomes fully complete from that seat alone; therefore even on one trident, in sacrifice, one should contemplate that established.

[tal-a16-v17] Not knowing the rite, knowing the procedure, thus spoken by Trishika; then in the middle, so on the right, on the left, on the peak, and everywhere.

[tal-a16-v18] One should worship as one self up to the world guardians' weapons, and as supreme; one should fully honor all deities.

[tal-a16-v19] The glorious lord, mother-presence, uninjured; then also by enjoyment sacrifice, the knowledge limb, the Bhairava octad.

[tal-a16-v20] The pair and wheel goddesses, in their own place, one should worship outside; world guardians with weapons, with sandal, flowers, drinks, and so on.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tata ājñāṃ gṛhītvā tu puṣpadhūpādipūjitam / pūjyamādhāraśaktyādi śūlamūlātprabhṛtyalam śivāntaṃ sitapadmānte triśūlānāṃ traye kramāt / madhyaśūle madhyagaḥ syātsadbhāvaḥ parayā saha vāme cāparayā sākaṃ navātmā dakṣagaṃ param / triśūle dakṣiṇe madhyaśṛṅgastho ratiśekharaḥ syātparāparayā sākaṃ dakṣe bhairavasatpare / vāme triśūle madhyastho navātmāparayā saha syātpare parayā sākaṃ vāmāre saṃśca bhairavaḥ / itthaṃ sarvagatatve śrīparādevyāḥ sthite sati yāgo bhavetsusaṃpūrṇastadadhiṣṭhānamātrataḥ / ekaśūle@pyato yāge cintayettadadhiṣṭhitam avidhijño vidhānajña ityevaṃ trīśikoditam / tato madhye tathā dakṣe vāme śṛṅge ca sarvataḥ lokapālāstraparyantamekātmatvena pūjayet / paratvena ca sarvāsāṃ devatānāṃ prapūjayet śrīmantaṃ mātṛsadbhāvabhaṭṭārakamanāmayam / tato@pi bhogayāgena vidyāṅgaṃ bhairavāṣṭakam yāmalaṃ cakradevīśca svasthāne pūjayedbahiḥ / lokapālānastrayutāngandhapuṣpāsavādibhiḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v21] One should worship with supreme devotion, free from wealth-deceit; then of pot, weapon, vase, circle, place, self.

[tal-a16-v22] One should do investigation of five from nondual meditation; but those who do not find that nondual pervasion, Shiva-natured.

[tal-a16-v23] By mantra channel application, they enter the nondual path; having exited by their own right from the circle-dwelling, from the left.

[tal-a16-v24] Having entered by another and exited, in pot place, in pitcher, in fire place, and thus in order, until in one's own left.

[tal-a16-v25] By root-investigation force, with prana-thread covering — thus unity-flashing self — pervasion-consciousness shines.

[tal-a16-v26] Then special worship, made of non-duality — steeped in Shiva-nondual nectar — that indeed is supreme.

[tal-a16-v27] By that — of the bound soul's argha flowers fragrance and liquor — the view of Shiva-nonduality is purification, supreme making.

[tal-a16-v28] Before the Lord one should offer living beings and elements arisen from that — perfected unperfected mixed, whatever moving or still.

[tal-a16-v29] Seen sprinkled witnessed, obtained and joined — extinguished hero-victim — he is eightfold supreme.

[tal-a16-v30] In order, never to be given to the unworthy — the Shiva-used oblation indeed not everyone is worthy to eat.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-pūjayetparayā bhaktyā vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ / tataḥ kumbhāstrakalaśīmaṇḍalasthānalātmanām pañcānāmanusandhānaṃ kuryādadvayabhāvanāt / ye tu tāmadvayavyāptiṃ na vindanti śivātmikām mantranāḍīprayogeṇa te viśantyadvaye pathi / svadakṣiṇena niḥsṛtya maṇḍalasthasya vāmataḥ praviśyānyena niḥsṛtya kumbhasthe karkarīgate / vahnisthe ca krameṇetthaṃ yāvatsvasminsvavāmataḥ mūlānusandhānabalātprāṇatantūmbhane sati / itthamaikyasphurattātmā vyāptisaṃvitprakāśate tato viśeṣapūjāṃ ca kuryādadvayabhāvitām / yacchivādvayapīyūṣasaṃsiktaṃ paramaṃ hi tat tenārghapuṣpagandhāderāsavasya paśoratha / yā śivādvayatādṛṣṭiḥ sā śuddhiḥ paramīkṛtiḥ nivedayedvibhoragre jīvāndhātūṃstadutthitān / siddhānasiddhānvyāmiśrānyadvā kiṃciccarācaram dṛṣṭaprokṣitasaṃdraṣṭṛprālabdhopāttayojitaḥ / nirvāpito vīrapaśuḥ so@ṣṭadhottaratottamaḥ yathottaraṃ na dātavyamayogyebhyaḥ kadācana / śivopayuktaṃ hi havirna sarvo bhoktumarhati

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v31] Whoever, though initiation-devoid, impelled by Shiva-will-rite, eats with devotion — complete, he would be a well-cultivated samayin.

[tal-a16-v32] Seen and looked upon indeed, by rays-kindled eye-offering — sprinkled only, moistened by argha-vessel drops.

[tal-a16-v33] The complete seer of the shown, fully worshipped mandala — commenced, purified by the spoken triad — he too should shake.

[tal-a16-v34] One would tremble, flow, stiffen, dissolve, in order — taken up in sacrifice-presence, pacified by weapons and winds.

[tal-a16-v35] Joined by cause-abandonment method, from Shiva-union — extinguished by practiced guru-life-breath-mind offering.

[tal-a16-v36] By southern fire, from gentle-kala-net dissolution — thus indeed at first, resort to the supreme form by becoming one.

[tal-a16-v37] Therefore, by fiery practice one should enter the flame-garland, and by the left path of the bound soul melt the moon-ray net with heat.

[tal-a16-v38] Resting in the navel wheel with breath-rays, becoming supreme by one's own power, one should here wrap the living being with the living being.

[tal-a16-v39] Heating by the sun of one's own consciousness, one should melt part by part; then quickly bring the net of parts to unity in the self.

[tal-a16-v40] With force, uproot from essence this karma-bound one who nourishes and completes all principles.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yastu dīkṣāvihīno@pi śivecchāvidhicoditaḥ / bhaktyāśnāti sa saṃpūrṇaḥ samayī syātsubhāvitaḥ dṛṣṭo@valokitaścaiva kiraṇeddhadṛgarpaṇāt / prokṣitaḥ kevalaṃ hyarghapātravipruḍbhirukṣitaḥ saṃdraṣṭā darśitāśeṣasamyakpūjitamaṇḍalaḥ / prālabdha uktatritayasaṃskṛtaḥ so@pi dhūnayet kampeta prasravetstabdhaḥ pralīno vā yathottaram / upātto yāgasānnidhye śamitaḥ śastramārutaiḥ yojitaḥ kāraṇatyāgakrameṇa śivayojanāt / nirvāpitaḥ kṛtābhyāsaguruprāṇamanorpaṇāt dakṣiṇenāgninā saumyakalājālavilāpanāt / tathāhyādau paraṃ rūpamekībhāvena saṃśrayet tasmādāgneyacāreṇa jvālāmālāmucāviśet / paśorvāmena candrāṃśujālaṃ tāpena gālayet nābhicakre@tha viśrāmyetprāṇaraśmigaṇaiḥ saha / paro bhūtvā svaśaktyātra jīvaṃ jīvena veṣṭayet svacitsūryeṇa saṃtāpya drāvayet kalāṃ kalām / tato drutaṃ kalājālaṃ prāpayyaikatvamātmani samastatattvasaṃpūrṇamāpyāyanavidhāyinam / unmūlayeta saṃrambhātkarmabaddhamamuṃ rasāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v41] Then, by the yoga of uprooting and unwrapping, revolving left, one becomes the nourisher of one's own breath, full of kundali nectar.

[tal-a16-v42] The filament of nectar from the heart lotus, taken by leftward circuit, melts the tissue by gaining ascent to the heart center.

[tal-a16-v43] Taking the pure moon essence, slightly red and yellow, into the breath-body that is like the tip of an elephant's trunk.

[tal-a16-v44] Having exited suddenly by the left path of one's own self, one should enter, nourishing the heart-lotus moon wheel called apāna.

[tal-a16-v45] That situated deity wheel should be nourished by that essence; by this method, all rasas, blood, and the rest are nourished.

[tal-a16-v46] One should gather the tissues in group sequence, one by one, or only in the middle of the collision of sun, moon, and fire.

[tal-a16-v47] Then, taking the living being that is light-form called breath-power, one should equalize the living being by the goddess wheel through meditation.

[tal-a16-v48] That itself is the chief nourishment: the identity of enjoyer and enjoyed; that great one is the fire-casket, blossoming, three-cornered, time-self.

[tal-a16-v49] When, in a half-ghatika sequence, rest-yoga occurs amid blood and similar essence-flow movements, the mass is present.

[tal-a16-v50] By a hundred repetitions, pacification of the bound soul occurs; having practiced there for some time with undivided mind.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tata unmūlanodveṣṭayogādvāmaṃ paribhraman / kuṇḍalyamṛtasaṃpūrṇasvakaprāṇaprasevakaḥ vāmāvartakramopāttahṛtpadmāmṛtakesaraḥ / hṛtkarṇikārūḍhilābhādojodhātuṃ vilāpitam śuddhasomātmakaṃ sāramīṣallohitapītalam / ādāya karihastāgrasadṛśe prāṇavigrahe niḥsṛtya jhaṭiti svātmavāmamārgeṇa saṃviśet / āpyāyayannapānākhyacandracakrahṛdambuje sthitaṃ taddevatācakraṃ tena sāreṇa tarpayet / anena vidhinā sarvānrasaraktādikāṃstathā dhātūnsamāharetsaṃghakramādekaikaśo@thavā / kevalaṃ tvathavāgnīnduravisaṃghaṭṭamadhyagam jyotīrūpamatha prāṇaśaktyākhyaṃ jīvamāharet / jīvaṃ samarasīkuryāddevīcakreṇa bhāvanāt tadeva tarpaṇaṃ mukhyaṃ bhogyabhoktrātmataiva sā / agnisaṃpuṭaphullārṇatryaśrakālātmako mahān piṇḍo raktādisāraughacālanākarṣaṇādiṣu / itthaṃ viśrāntiyogena ghaṭikārdhakrame sati āvṛttiśatayogena paśornirvāpaṇaṃ bhavet / kṛtvā katipayaṃ kālaṃ tatrābhyāsamananyadhīḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v51] As stated in the Cintamani, by that form the yogi obtains siddhi without doubt; that secret is clear like prana.

[tal-a16-v52] Even for an unseen bound soul, the rite is thus; entered into the sacrificial ground, he is killed there and accomplished.

[tal-a16-v53] One joined to the cakra there is called a hero-victim; but one killed elsewhere is treated by totality or partly.

[tal-a16-v54] Offered to the deity, that is indeed held to be an external victim; kingdom, gain, stability, devotion to Shiva, and identity with that follow.

[tal-a16-v55] Shiva-knowledge, attainment of the mantra-world, retinue, and union with that belong to the bound soul by equality from external or hero dharma.

[tal-a16-v56] Flowers and the like also share that gain; by Shiva worship, one means, the lord of gods is of the nature of blessing the universe.

[tal-a16-v57] By sacrifice alone he blesses; what is not moving and still? Therefore even a non-hero, though joined with doubt and the like, is compassionate.

[tal-a16-v58] Never adopt a harming thought in the victim rite; this is a great benefit to the bound soul, though it may be unpleasant at that time.

[tal-a16-v59] Disease-cutting, medicine, austerity, and use are an example here; as stated in the glorious Mrtyunjaya, bond-cutting is done for the bound soul.

[tal-a16-v60] By separation from the three impurities the body does not grow; by cutting the mass of merit and demerit the body falls away indeed.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yathā cintāmaṇau proktaṃ tena rūpeṇa yogavit / niḥśaṅkaḥ siddhimāpnoti gopyaṃ tatprāṇavatsphuṭam parokṣe@pi paśāvevaṃ vidhiḥ syādyojanaṃ prati / praveśito yāgabhuvi hatastatraiva sādhitaḥ cakrajuṣṭaśca tatraiva sa vīrapaśurucyate / yastvanyatrāpi nihataḥ sāmastyenāṃśato@pivā devāya vinivedyeta sa vai bāhyapaśurmataḥ / rājyaṃ lābho@tha tatsthairyaṃ śive bhaktistadātmatā śivajñānaṃ mantralokaprāptistatparivāratā / tatsāyujyaṃ paśoḥ sāmyādbāhyādervīradharmaṇaḥ puṣpādayo@pi tallābhabhāginaḥ śivapūjayā / ekopāyena deveśo viśvānugrahaṇātmakaḥ yāgenaivānugṛhṇāti kiṃ kiṃ yanna carācaram / tenāvīro@pi śaṅkādiyuktaḥ kāruṇiko@pica na hiṃsābuddhimādadhyātpaśukarmaṇi jātucit / paśormahopakāro@yaṃ tadātve@pyapriyaṃ bhavet vyādhicchedauṣadhatapoyojanātra nidarśanam / śrīmanmṛtyuñjaye proktaṃ pāśacchede kṛte paśoḥ malatrayaviyogena śarīraṃ na prarohati / dharmādharmaughavicchedāccharīraṃ cyacate kila

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v61] By that this killing is not so called — initiation is variegated-formed; of the fetter-bound, separation from breaths is indeed killing.

[tal-a16-v62] But this is yojana only — of the beast for the god, in offering; therefore relying on the god's word: give many beasts, thus.

[tal-a16-v63] Offered, body regained, offered again — six times thus — whoever here is the six-birth supreme beast.

[tal-a16-v64] As gold purified by the firing process is proclaimed — what perfection would he not himself bestow, or is he not liberated?

[tal-a16-v65] It is said in the Ananda scripture: who abandons mantra-consecration, reviles initiations, gives goddesses and mantras without rule, leads astray.

[tal-a16-v66] Having gained initiation-mantra and the rest, deluded by son and the rest he abandons — then attaining humanity, he does so again.

[tal-a16-v67] Thus from one to seven births — twofold, two-footed or four-footed — the beast is born for goddess-oblation purpose.

[tal-a16-v68] Given by the giver, through that door he goes from union to Shiva — thus considering, strange is the employment of beasts.

[tal-a16-v69] The desired-to-be-enjoyed should not be made into that beast elsewhere — nor is this one suitable — so understanding, remove it.

[tal-a16-v70] But if desire is for that beast in particular, then offer it — give so many beasts, as said by Maheshin.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tenaitanmāraṇaṃ noktaṃ dīkṣeyaṃ citrarūpiṇī / rūḍhapāśasya yaḥ prāṇairviyogo māraṇaṃ hi tat iyaṃ tu yojanaiva syātpaśordevāya tarpaṇe / tasmāddevoktimāśritya paśūndadyādbahūniti niveditaḥ punaḥprāptadeho bhūyoniveditaḥ / ṣaṭkṛtva itthaṃ yaḥ so@tra ṣaḍjanmā paśuruttamaḥ yathā pākakramācchuddhaṃ hema tadvatsa kīrtitaḥ / kāṃ siddhiṃ naiva vitaretsvayaṃ kiṃvā na mucyate uktaṃ tvānandaśāstre yo mantrasaṃskāravāṃstyajet / samayānkutsayeddevīrdadyānmantrānvinā nayāt dīkṣāmantrādikaṃ prāpya tyajetputrādimohitaḥ / tato manuṣyatāmetya punarevaṃ karotyapi itthamekādisaptāntajanmāsau dvividho dvipāt / catuṣpādvā paśurdevīcarukārthaṃ prajāyate dātrarpito@sau taddvārā yāti sāyujyataḥ śivam / iti saṃbhāvya citraṃ tatpaśūnāṃ praviceṣṭitam bhogyīcikīrṣitaṃ naiva kuryādanyatra taṃ paśum / nāpi naiṣa bhavedyogya iti buddhvāpasārayet taṃ paśuṃ kiṃtu kāṅkṣā cedviśeṣe taṃ tu ḍhaukayet / tāvatastānpaśūndadyāttathācoktaṃ maheśinā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v71] The beast's omentum and marrow, melted, from amid fire — offer to the Shakti-wheel; considered supreme offering.

[tal-a16-v72] Heart interior head shoulder liver chiefly offer — ear-coil marrow axe, the more principal — and also that.

[tal-a16-v73] Then the teacher should perform the offering to the mantra circle, offer that, and then inform the lord.

[tal-a16-v74] As guru, I am known by you, supreme lord, through direct dream instruction and chants from the guru's mouth.

[tal-a16-v75] Disciples impelled by Shiva's power are to be favored by you; these of that kind have obtained from them, doing favor.

[tal-a16-v76] Absorb me by your own self rays, so that I become Shiva; then welcome Shiva's word.

[tal-a16-v77] One should remember the self as not different from Shiva, doer of five acts, instrument of own self, mantras and form, with desire to protect.

[tal-a16-v78] Then, having bound the white turban, worship the hands in order, mutually, for burning bonds and emitting pure principle.

[tal-a16-v79] By light form, worship mantras in Shiva's hand, excluding womb covering, song, limb, attendant, and seat.

[tal-a16-v80] Afterward meditate on the self alone, like the moon in water; different by action condition, but sixfold different only apparently, in reality one.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-paśorvapāmedasī ca gālite vahnimadhyataḥ / arpayecchakticakrāya paramaṃ tarpaṇaṃ matam hṛdantramuṇḍāṃsayakṛtpradhānaṃ vinivedayet / karṇikākuṇḍalīmajjaparśu mukhyataraṃ ca vā tato@gnau tarpaṇaṃ kuryānmantracakrasya daiśikaḥ / tannivedya ca devāya tato vijñāpayetprabhum gurutvena tvayaivāhamājñātaḥ parameśvara / sākṣātsvapnopadeśādyairjapairgurumukhena vā anugrāhyāstvayā śiṣyāḥ śivaśaktipracoditāḥ / tadete tadvidhāḥ prāptāstvamebhyaḥ kurvanugraham samāveśaya māṃ svātmaraśmibhiryadahaṃ śivaḥ / evaṃ bhavatviti tataḥ śivoktimabhinandayet śivābhinnamathātmānaṃ pañcakṛtyakaraṃ smaret / svātmanaḥ karaṇaṃ mantrānmūrtiṃ cānujighṛkṣayā tato baddhvā sitoṣṇīṣaṃ hastayorarcayetkramāt / anyonyaṃ pāśadāhāya śuddhatattvavisṛṣṭaye tejorūpeṇa mantrāṃśca śivahaste samarcayet / garbhāvaraṇagānaṅgaparivārāsanojjhitān ātmānaṃ bhāvayetpaścādekakaṃ jalacandravat / kṛtyopādhivaśādbhinnaṃ ṣoḍhābhinnaṃ tu vastutaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v81] I am in the circle, witness of all actions; pure seeing indeed is imagined by me in Shambhu's circle.

[tal-a16-v82] As fire-rite subject, I am situated in fire; when the self is kindled, mantras would be capable of the bond-burning rite.

[tal-a16-v83] World lords called by common light form are satisfied and made to hear; they extend the small one's authority.

[tal-a16-v84] Up to the end of sacrifice I am established in the pot for obstacle peace; common form thereby nourishes particular forms.

[tal-a16-v85] In the disciple's body, he indeed acts as if shaking off bonds by his own will, for establishing loosening of that bond.

[tal-a16-v86] I am directly abiding in my own body, doer of grace acts, and skillful in initiation due to freedom of knowledge and action.

[tal-a16-v87] Connected to circles of senses and acts, one, as I am sixfold fire and so on, clearly so.

[tal-a16-v88] Having considered thus, by which path initiation is desired for connection, except the disciple, in five, him should one worship.

[tal-a16-v89] At the end of connection strength, and by difference of summary and expansion, one should make it fully practiced and filled by inclusion of others.

[tal-a16-v90] Then also by thought one should connect more to Shiva-nature: I alone am the supreme principle, and not like a path anywhere.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-maṇḍalastho@hamevāyaṃ sākṣī cākhilakarmaṇām / śuddhā hi draṣṭṛtā śambhormaṇḍale kalpitā mayā homādhikaraṇatvena vahnāvahamavasthitaḥ / yadātmateddhā mantrāḥ syuḥ pāśaploṣavidhāvalam sāmānyatejorūpāntarāhūtā bhuvaneśvarāḥ / tarpitāḥ śrāvitāścāṇornādhikāraṃ pratanvate ā yāgāntamahaṃ kumbhe saṃsthito vighnaśāntaye / sāmānyarūpatā yena viśeṣāpyāyakāriṇī śiṣyadehe ca tatpāśaśithilatvaprasiddhaye / sa hi svecchāvaśātpāśānvidhunvanniva vartate sākṣātsvadehasaṃstho@haṃ kartānugrahakarmaṇām / jñānakriyāsvatantratvāddīkṣākarmaṇi peśalaḥ bhinnakāryākṛtivrātendriyacakrānusandhimān / eko yathāhaṃ vahnyādiṣaḍrūpo@smi tathā sphuṭam evamālocya yenaiṣo@dhvanā dīkṣāṃ cikīrṣati / anusaṃhitaye śiṣyavarjaṃ pañcasu taṃ yajet anusandhibalānte ca samāsavyāsabhedataḥ / kuryādatyantamabhyastamanyāntarbhāvapūritam tato@pi cintayā bhūyo@nusandadhyācchivātmatām / ahameva paraṃ tattvaṃ naca paddhaṭavat kvacit

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v100] This threefold rite has limits at the forehead, the hole, and the twelve-end.

[tal-a16-v91] By that great light, all this world is in me, and it is not projected by anyone like an external reflection.

[tal-a16-v92] I am maker of this; it is not dependent on another and is established by me; thus purified by experience of great pervasion.

[tal-a16-v93] A creature having gone to equality with me is called liberated; by succession of heating, rubbing, pouring and so on, fire-nature.

[tal-a16-v94] Like an iron ball goes, the guru thus to Shiva-nature; then standing before, or a previously manifested form.

[tal-a16-v95] In indirect initiation, or fashioned by kusha etc, the dead disciple having been seen and worshipped, one should place his path with flowers and so on.

[tal-a16-v96] By which path the teacher primarily desires initiation, having placed him in the body, there other should be included; this is the rule.

[tal-a16-v97] When the path to be purified has been placed, the purifier mantra is placed there as desired, according to the propriety of the thing purified.

[tal-a16-v98] Sometimes, without placing the thing to be purified, mere placement of the purifier makes it pure itself; what is purified becomes pure by the purifier's power.

[tal-a16-v99] By wish one may use another, parapara, or para rite; having resorted according to their combination, one performs nyasa of the six paths.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-mahāprakāśastattena mayi sarvamidaṃ jagat / naca tatkenacidbāhyapratibimbavadarpitam kartāhamasya tannānyādhīnaṃ ca madadhiṣṭhitam / itthaṃbhūtamahāvyāptisaṃvedanapavitritaḥ matsamatvaṃ gato janturmukta ityabhidhīyate / tāpanirgharṣasekādipāramparyeṇa vahnitām yathāyogolako yāti gururevaṃ śivātmatām / tataḥ puraḥsthitaṃ yadvā purobhāvitavigraham parokṣadīkṣaṇe yadvā darbhādyaiḥ kalpite mṛte / śiṣye vīkṣyārcya puṣpādyairnyasedadhvānamasya tam yenādhvanā mukhyatayā dīkṣāmicchati daiśikaḥ / taṃ dehe nyasya tatrāntarbhāvyamanyaditi sthitiḥ śodhyādhvani ca vinyaste tatraiva pariśodhakam / nyasedyathepsitaṃ mantraṃ śodhyaucityānusārataḥ kvacicchodhyaṃ tvavinyasya śodhakanyāsamātrataḥ / svayaṃ śuddhyati saṃśodhyaṃ śodhakasya prabhāvataḥ aparaṃ parāparaṃ ca paraṃ ca vidhimicchayā / tadyojanānusāreṇa śritvā nyāsaḥ ṣaḍadhvanaḥ lalāṭāntaṃ vedavasau randhrāntaṃ rasarandhrake / vasukhendau dvādaśāntamityeṣa trividho vidhiḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v101] It is described in order in the treatise named Sripurva; there placement in the principles is at the ankle-end, four angulas.

[tal-a16-v102] Earth and the elements up to the root-end are measured two angulas each in order; above the navel it is six angulas.

[tal-a16-v103] For a man, the six principles are placed three angulas each, ending at the throat pit, eighteen angulas in all.

[tal-a16-v104] Sadashiva to the end and the four maya principles are measured four angulas each from the specified place.

[tal-a16-v105] One should remember the shiva principle, then the tejo form, unagitated, pervading all within and without.

[tal-a16-v106] The parapara rite measures from water to the end with a pair and a root of three angulas, with a twelve-angula excess.

[tal-a16-v107] If unmanifest, the para rite measures from water to the end in three angulas in the four, with twenty-four excess, eight hundred.

[tal-a16-v108] The threefold measure is manifest from the vasu directions and sun decay, as also said in the maya tantra, according to desire for each fruit.

[tal-a16-v109] In the nyasa of nine, five, four, and one tattvas, one should arrange the nyasa oneself by intellect, so long as one contemplates the inclusion of tattvas.

[tal-a16-v110] By this very five-kala egg nyasa is indicated; and in Trishira Tantra it is said to be situated in its own support as it stands.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-krameṇa kathyate dṛṣṭaḥ śāstre śrīpūrvasaṃjñite / tatra tattveṣu vinyāso gulphānte caturaṅgule dharā jalādimūlāntaṃ pratyekaṃ dvyaṅgulaṃ kramāt / rasaśrutyaṅgulaṃ nābherūrdhvamitthaṃ ṣaḍaṅgule puṃsaḥ kalāntaṃ ṣaṭtattvīṃ pratyekaṃ tryaṅgule kṣipet / aṣṭādaśāṅgulaṃ tvevaṃ kaṇṭhakūpāvasānakam sadāśivāntaṃ māyādicatuṣkaṃ caturaṅgule / pratyekamityabdhivasusaṃkhyamālikadeśataḥ śivatattvaṃ tataḥ paścāttejorūpamanākulam / sarveṣāṃ vyāpakatvena sabāhyābhyantaraṃ smaret jalāddhyantaṃ sārdhayugmaṃ mūlaṃ tryaṅgulamityataḥ / dvādaśāṅgulatādhikyādvidhireṣa parāparaḥ jalāddhyantaṃ tryaṅgule cedavyaktaṃ tu catuṣṭaye / taccaturviṃśatyādhikyātparo@pyaṣṭaśate vidhiḥ trividhonmānakaṃ vyaktaṃ vasudigbhyo ravikṣayāt / mayatantre tathācoktaṃ tattatsvaphalavāñchayā navapañcacatustryekatattvanyāse svayaṃ dhiyā / nyāsaṃ prakalpayettāvattattvāntarbhāvacintanāt kalāpañcakavedāṇḍanyāso@nenaiva lakṣitaḥ / uktaṃ ca triśirastantre svādhārasthaṃ yathāsthitam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v111] The rise is twelve angulas beyond the body, equal; then seventy-two ten and two are in the body from the head end.

[tal-a16-v112] Starting from the feet, O fair-hipped one, up to the anahata region, even beyond the body, by rest of consciousness, by force of imagination.

[tal-a16-v113] Body-ness thus; therefore the rise should be twelve angulas; thus to determine here this is said one hundred eight.

[tal-a16-v114] Then city nyasa up to the ankle: earth; here sixteen cities; therefore by one-angula pervasion each from Lakula onward.

[tal-a16-v115] Up to the two testicles, three angulas; but goat-testicle then in oceans; in eight deva-yogas two indeed from each angula foot.

[tal-a16-v116] Thus up to pradhana forty-six angulas; fifty-six cities thus; but in eastern ground sixteen.

[tal-a16-v117] Then by half-angula pervasion, six cities in three angulas; four, pair; in one one; and city in angula.

[tal-a16-v118] In attachment, male cities lord number thus; in six angulas; in anger-lord city one in pair; and this anda; and know.

[tal-a16-v119] Of Samvarta and Jyotisha thus, of kala and tattva in order, of Shura and Pancanta cities fixed, and one-pair-ness.

[tal-a16-v120] In Shri Purva Shastra that is said by supreme lord Shambhu: from northward order two-one difference in vidya etc three.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-dvādaśāṅgulamutthānaṃ dehātītaṃ samaṃ tataḥ / dvāsaptatirdaśa dve ca dehasthaṃ śiraso@ntataḥ pādādārabhya suśroṇi anāhatapadāvadhi / dehātīte@pi viśrāntyā saṃvitteḥ kalpanāvaśāt dehatvamiti tasmātsyādutthānaṃ dvādaśāṅgulam / iti nirṇetumatraitaduktamaṣṭottaraṃ śatam puranyāso@tha gulphāntaṃ bhūḥ purāṇyatra ṣoḍaśa / tasmādekāṅgulavyāptyā pratyekaṃ lakulāditaḥ dviraṇḍāntaṃ tryaṅgulaṃ tu cchagalāṇḍamathābdhiṣu / devayogāṣṭake dve hi pratyekāṅgulapādataḥ iti pradhānaparyantaṃ ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadaṅgulam / ṣaṭpañcāśatpurāṇītthaṃ prāgdharāyāṃ tu ṣoḍaśa tato@pyardhāṅgulavyāptyā ṣaṭpurāṇyaṅgulatraye / catvāri yugma ekasminnekaṃ ca puramaṅgule sarāge puṃspurāṇīśasaṃkhyānītthaṃ ṣaḍaṅgule / krodheśapuramekasmindvaye cāṇḍamiyaṃ ca vit saṃvartajyotiṣorevaṃ kalātattvagayoḥ kramāt / śūrapañcāntapurayorniyatau caikayugmatā śrīpūrvaśāstre taccoktaṃ parameśena śaṃbhunā / uttarādikramādadvyekabhedo vidyādike traye

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v121] Because order lacks essence at the beginning, niyati comes before kalā, or the two principles are designated by mutual names.

[tal-a16-v122] The arrangement of Ekavīra, Śikheśa, and Śrīkaṇṭha before time is described as niyati.

[tal-a16-v123] Thus the six principles beginning with puruṣa are seen designated by mutual names and arranged in eighteen angulas.

[tal-a16-v124] Then the eight principles standing in māyā, each half an angula, occupy four angulas up to thumb measure.

[tal-a16-v125] Thus twenty-eight cities are in two eyes; three cities come from puruṣa at night, two are less by one-third angula, in order.

[tal-a16-v126] Two and two make five cities in vidyā in four angulas; then eight aiśa cities follow in four half-angulas in order.

[tal-a16-v127] Then three in two and two thus in four; sādāśiva is fivefold, and one vasu is in the sun.

[tal-a16-v128] Sixteenfold rasa-viśikha, two vasu, vasu-moon thus; city groups are four, rasa-ocean, pair-eye, and suns there, with angulas in order.

[tal-a16-v129] One hundred eighteen cities are arranged in this body measured as eighty-four; thus in the remainder is the pervading śiva principle.

[tal-a16-v130] Thus another method, called parāpara, is described; its enumeration of eight arrows, made by the sky sage, is to be known in the next method.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-asāratvātkramasyādau niyatiḥ parataḥ kalā / athavānyonyasaṃjñābhyāṃ tattvayorvyapadeśyatā ekavīraśikheśaśrīkaṇṭhāḥ kāle trayastraye / kālasya pūrvaṃ vinyāso niyaterabhidhīyate athavānyonyasaṃjñābhirvyapadeśo hi dṛśyate / evaṃ pumādiṣaṭtattvī vinyastāṣṭādaśāṅgule tato@pyaṅguṣṭhamātrāntaṃ māyātattvasthamaṣṭakam / pratyekamardhāṅgulataḥ syādaṅgulacatuṣṭaye itthaṃ dvyakṣṇi purāṇyaṣṭāviṃśatiḥ puruṣānniśi / puratrayaṃ dvayostryaṃśanyūnāṅgulamiti kramāt dvayordvayaṃ pañcapurī vaidyīye caturaṅgule / tata aiśapurāṇyaṣṭau catuṣke@rdhāṅgulakramāt tatastrīṇi dvaye dve ca dvayoritthaṃ catuṣṭaye / sādāśivaṃ pañcakaṃ syāditthaṃ vasvekakaṃ ravau ṣoḍaśakaṃ rasaviśikhaṃ vasudvikaṃ vasuśaśīti puravargāḥ / vedā rasābdhi yugmākṣi ca ravayastatra cāṅgulāḥ kramaśaḥ aṣṭādaśādhikaśataṃ purāṇi dehe@tra caturaśītimite / vinyastāni taditthaṃ śeṣe tu vyāpakaṃ śivaṃ tattvam iti vidhiraparaḥ kathitaḥ parāparākhyo rasaśrutisthāne / aṣṭaśaraṃ saṃkhyānaṃ khamunikṛtaṃ tatpare vidhau jñeyam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v131] From Lakula to the end of eight yogas here, the world group's share is increased by counting in the two methods in order.

[tal-a16-v132] Then in the three methods from aparā, the placement of the foot-path is said as ten-footed before; it is placed independently when.

[tal-a16-v133] Initiation is performed by that very means; if nyasa is to be given, its arrangement follows the primary tattva order in initiation, and the word sequence is set accordingly.

[tal-a16-v134] According to each tattva, the procedure is included therein; when self-predominance applies, the word procedure in initiation is adjusted accordingly.

[tal-a16-v135] Nyasa should be placed in order across groups of four, eight, eight, ten, and ten, not merely as tattva recitation.

[tal-a16-v136] In groups of ten, fifteen, veda, and moon, the earth word and navapadi are situated in the matrika garland.

[tal-a16-v137] The pervader should join the tenth word, called Shiva, while excluding the earth word and five other words.

[tal-a16-v138] There are two rules; placing twelve finger lengths follows the same rule for the mantra path in placement and joining.

[tal-a16-v139] Only pervasion differs, as stated before; thus the placement of the letter path is told here among three rules.

[tal-a16-v140] One in four, each with two fingers in order; twenty-three letters should be, with six letters one by one in three.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-lakulāderyogāṣṭakaparyantasyātra bhuvanapūgasya / adhikīkuryādgaṇanāvaśena bhāgaṃ vidhidvaye kramaśaḥ aparādividhitraitādatha nyāsaḥ padādhvanaḥ / pūrvaṃ daśapadī coktā svatantrā nyasyate yadā tayaiva dīkṣā kāryā cettadeyaṃ nyāsakalpanā / tattvādimukhyatāyogāddīkṣāyāṃ tu padāvalī tattattvādyanusāreṇa tatrāntarbhāvyate tathā / svapradhānatvayoge tu dīkṣāyāṃ padapaddhatim nyasyetkrameṇa tattvādivadanānavalokinīm / caturṣvaṣṭāsu cāṣṭāsu daśasvatha daśasvatha daśasvatho pañcadaśasvatha vedaśarenduṣu / dharāpadānnavapadīṃ mātṛkāmālinīgatām yojayedvyāptṛ daśamaṃ padaṃ tu śivasaṃjñitam / dharāpadaṃ varjayitvā pañca yāni padāni tu vidhidvayaṃ syānnikṣipya dvādaśa dvādaśāṅgulān / mantrādhvano@pyeṣa eva vidhirvinyāsayojane vyāptimātraṃ hi bhidyetetyuktaṃ prāgeva tattathā / varṇādhvano@tha vinyāsaḥ kathyate@tra vidhitraye ekaṃ caturṣu pratyekaṃ dvayoraṅgulayoḥ kramāt / trayoviṃśativarṇī syāt ṣaḍvarṇyekaikaśastriṣu

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v141] Then four in four in reverse order; the matrika garland letters should be, and the pervader is the Shaiva one from mercury moon.

[tal-a16-v142] Excluding the first letter, a tattva-like ravi-nine arrangement should be; in twenty-three letters, another two rules also apply.

[tal-a16-v143] In the previous scripture, three rules were first stated in the tattvas; they are extended, and in two letters, different and same, it is equal.

[tal-a16-v144] Even though letters are two-fold, a six-fold difference is said; it is to be known ultimately by the tattva path rule.

[tal-a16-v145] By instruction and extension, what was said in those words is again indicated there indeed, in our Heart-Lord scripture.

[tal-a16-v146] Of pada mantra kala and the rest, per the previous sutra, make threefold-ness by the tattva-varṇa-spoken path.

[tal-a16-v147] Said in tat-pada-mantras; and in kalas it is determined — in four, in six-and-taste-veda, in twenty-two, and in twelve.

[tal-a16-v148] Four beginning with Nivṛtti pervade; the peace-transcending may hold — in the second kala, twelve twelves of angulas.

[tal-a16-v149] In order having thrown the higher-lower-higher rule-duality — here by the four-egg-rite-beginning word it is grasped.

[tal-a16-v150] By the four-kala'd, speak therein the three rites — thus the sixfold path, in the disciple-body to be purified, before.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-pratyekamatha catvāraścaturṣviti vilomataḥ / mālinīmātṛkārṇāḥ syurvyāptṛ śaivaṃ rasendutaḥ varjayitvādyavarṇaṃ tu tattvavatsyādravīnnavīn / tāṃ trayoviṃśatau varṇeṣvapyanyatsyādvidhidvayam śrīpūrvaśāstre tenādau tattveṣūktaṃ vidhitrayam / atidiṣṭaṃ tu tadbhinnābhinnavarṇadvaye samam dvividho@pi hi varṇānāṃ ṣaḍvidho bheda ucyate / tattvamārgavidhānena jñātavyaḥ paramārthataḥ upadeśātideśābhyāṃ yaduktaṃ tatpadādiṣu / bhūyo@tidiṣṭaṃ tatraiva śāstre@smaddhṛdayeśvare padamantrakalādīnāṃ pūrvasūtrānusārataḥ / tritayatvaṃ prakurvīta tattvavarṇoktavartmanā uktaṃ tatpadamantreṣu kalāsvatha nirūpyate / caturṣu rasavede dvāviṃśatau dvādaśasvatha nivṛttyādyāścatasraḥ syurvyāptrī syācchāntyatītikā / dvitīyasyāṃ kalāyāṃ tu dvādaśa dvādaśāṅgulān kramātkṣiptvā vidhidvaitaṃ parāparaparātmakam / caturaṇḍavidhistvādiśabdeneha pragṛhyate kalācatuṣkavattena tasminvācyaṃ vidhitrayam / evaṃ ṣaḍvidhamadhvānaṃ śodhyaśiṣyatanau purā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v151] Installing one as primary, install the purifier-approved — the path-seat-mantra-flood is the purifier, indeed one, from the beginning.

[tal-a16-v152] Word-mass and garlanded, whole and scattered, in two ways — by single-hero state, or the sixfold from pair-union.

[tal-a16-v153] Five-faced, from sakti-and-that difference sixfold, again twofold — as single and paired, thus she is twelve-natured.

[tal-a16-v154] Six-limbed, twofold from all-otherness, again like mouth — multiplied by twelve-ness, twenty-four-divided.

[tal-a16-v155] In the eight beginning with Aghoras two, and a third from yamala-rise — and the mothers-true-being mantra alone, śruti-circle-going.

[tal-a16-v156] By one-two-three-four divisions thirteen-fold-natured — by single-hero quality this stands as fourteen-fold.

[tal-a16-v157] The fourfold wheel of unnameable withdrawal, stability, and creation is augmented by the goddesses' own mother-existence.

[tal-a16-v158] Thus seventy mantras are remembered; in six half-treatises and in the glorious sara treatise it is taught.

[tal-a16-v159] Here the wise purify by eight beginning with aghora, or by one-syllable mantras, or by the mother sequence.

[tal-a16-v160] Or by the bhairavi heart, or by the khechari heart, or by bhairava, O great goddess; then by the five face-limb groups.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-nyasyaikatamamukhyatvānnyasyecchodhakasaṃmatam / adhvanyāsanamantraughaḥ śodhako hyeka āditaḥ śabdarāśirmālinī ca samastavyastato dvidhā / ekavīratayā yadvā ṣaṭkaṃ yāmalayogataḥ pañcavaktrī śaktitadvadbhedātṣoḍhā punardvidhā / ekākiyāmalatvenetyevaṃ sā dvādaśātmikā ṣaḍaṅgī sakalānyatvāddvividhā vaktravatpunaḥ / dvādaśatvena guṇitā caturviṃśatibhedikā aghorādyaṣṭake dve ca tṛtīyaṃ yāmalodayāt / mātṛsadbhāvamantraśca kevalaḥ śruticakragaḥ ekadvitricaturbhedāttrayodaśabhidātmakaḥ / ekavīratayā so@yaṃ caturdaśatayā sthitaḥ anāmasaṃhṛtisthairyasṛṣṭicakraṃ caturvidham / devatābhirnijābhistanmātṛsadbhāvavṛṃhitam itthaṃ śodhakavargo@yaṃ mantrāṇāṃ saptatiḥ smṛtā / ṣaḍardhaśāstreṣu śrīmatsāraśāstre ca kathyate aghorādyaṣṭakeneha śodhanīyaṃ vipaścitā / athavaikākṣarāmantrairathavā mātṛkākramāt bhairavīyahṛdā vāpi khecarīhṛdayena vā / bhairaveṇa mahādevi tvatha vaktrāṅgapañcakaiḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v161] By whichever mantra creation in this tantra is made, by that alone the mantra-knower should initiate; thus is the supreme command.

[tal-a16-v162] Thus seventy kinds are declared by purifier difference; when initiation with these mantras occurs without purifying nyasa.

[tal-a16-v163] Then it is to be known seventyfold, devoid of birth and so on; the purifiable difference is then to be stated, and that too is told in brief.

[tal-a16-v164] Tattva is fourfold from differences of one, three, five, six, and thirty-six; path and likewise four egg groups are from five and one differences.

[tal-a16-v165] Thus the purifiable is tenfold; thirtyfold from the threefold rule of that; by purifiable-purifier difference, hundreds and twenty-one.

[tal-a16-v166] Here too, by nyasa union, in purifiable sound and action, one hundred twenty-one kinds, devoid of birth and so on, becomes.

[tal-a16-v167] Consisting of birth and so on, thus in hundredfold scripture, scripture would be seventy plus; that also from substance-knowledge difference.

[tal-a16-v168] Twofold; eighty-five would be hundreds plus eleven; from enjoyment-liberation inquiry twofold, that is declared.

[tal-a16-v169] Purification of both inauspicious and auspicious things makes enjoyment twofold, with distinction across three times.

[tal-a16-v170] Through one, two, or all powers, enjoyment becomes seven or eightfold, and guru-disciple order divides it twofold.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yena yena hi mantreṇa tantre@sminnudbhavaḥ kṛtaḥ / tenaiva dīkṣayenmantrī ityājñā pārameśvarī evaṃ śodhakabhedena saptatiḥ kīrtitā bhidaḥ / śodhyanyāsaṃ vinā mantrairetairdīkṣā yadā bhavet tadā saptatidhā jñeyā jananādivivarjitā / śodhyabhedo@tha vaktavyaḥ saṃkṣepātso@pi kathyate ekatripañcaṣaṭtriṃśadbhedāttāttvaścaturvidhaḥ / pañcaikabhedāccādhvānastathaivāṇḍacatuṣṭayam evaṃ daśavidhaṃ śodhyaṃ triṃśaddhā tadvidhitrayāt / śodhyaśodhakabhedena śatāni tvekaviṃśatiḥ atrāpi nyāsayogena śodhye@dhvani tathākṛteḥ / śataikaviṃśatibhidā jananādyujjhitā bhavet jananādimayī tāvatyevaṃ śatadṛśi śrutiḥ / syātsaptatyadhikā sāpi dravyavijñānabhedataḥ dvidheti pañcāśītiḥ syācchatānyadhikakhābdhikā / bhogamokṣānusandhānāddvividhā sā prakīrtitā aśubhasyaiva saṃśuddhyā śubhasyāpyatha śodhanāt / dvidhā bhogaḥ śubhe śuddhiḥ kālatrayavibhedini ekadvisāmastyavaśātsaptadhetyaṣṭadhā bhujiḥ / guruśiṣyakramātso@pi dvidhetyevaṃ vibhidyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v171] Because direct initiation depends on continuity between two, its result is full; disagreement brings ruin.

[tal-a16-v172] In indirect immortal initiation, the guru alone, by the glory of action and knowledge, leads the disciple to the desired abode.

[tal-a16-v173] When action and knowledge are undivided, their continuity is likewise; action is again divided because it is of that nature.

[tal-a16-v174] The holy Svachanda treatise says result differs by impression distinction for disciples and guru, even when action and the rest are undivided.

[tal-a16-v175] Variety exists in enjoyment because continuity between purifier and purified produces such variety, and variety is the life of distinction.

[tal-a16-v176] Thus the path purified by those same mouths is joined; wishing to enjoy some principle, he becomes enjoyer endowed with that power.

[tal-a16-v177] Here, if auspicious actions exist, enjoyment variegation is such; in action purification, variegation is otherwise.

[tal-a16-v178] Enjoyment is joined by immediate exit or by body, then by practice or at body's end; thus it is fourfold.

[tal-a16-v179] The previous eight-division is said to become thirty-two through yoga; liberation, though one, is the seed called convention.

[tal-a16-v180] For child and known quick death, devoid of power; for aged or powerful, aiming; purification is twofold by purification or non-purification.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-pratyakṣadīkṣaṇe yasmāddvayorekānusandhitaḥ / tādṛgdīkṣāphalaṃ pūrṇaṃ visaṃvāde tu viplavaḥ parokṣamṛtadīkṣādau gururevānusandhimān / kriyājñānamahimnā taṃ śiṣyaṃ dhāmnīpsite nayet avibhinne kriyājñāne karmaśuddhau tathaiva te / anusandhiḥ punarbhinnaḥ karma yasmāttadātmakam śrīmatsvacchandaśāstre ca vāsanābhedataḥ phalam / śiṣyāṇāṃ ca guroścoktamabhinne@pi kriyādike bhogasya śodhakācchodhyādanusandheśca tādṛśāt / vaicitryamasti bhedasya vaicitryaprāṇatā yataḥ tathāhi vaktrairyasyādhvā śuddhastaireva yojitaḥ / bhoktumiṣṭe kvacittattve sa bhoktā tadbalānvitaḥ śubhānāṃ karmaṇāṃ cātra sadbhāve bhogacitratā / tādṛgeva bhavetkarmaśuddhau tvanyaiva citratā bhogaśca sadya+utkrāntyā dehenaivātha saṃgataḥ / tadaivābhyāsato vāpi dehānte vetyasau catuḥ prāktanāṣṭabhidā yogāddvātriṃśadbheda ucyate / mokṣa eko@pi bījasya samayākhyasya tādṛśam bālādikaṃ jñātaśīghramaraṇaṃ śaktivarjitam / vṛddhaṃ voddiśya śaktaṃ vā śodhanāśodhanāddvidhā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v181] Mahesha speaks a command in the glorious cave concerning the guru's duty when death is near.

[tal-a16-v182] Seeing a disciple afflicted by old age and disease, the guru should transfer him and place him in the supreme principle.

[tal-a16-v183] Thirty-five distinctions of the guru, or of guru and disciple, are declared; seventy arise from the stated twofold calculation.

[tal-a16-v184] Having destroyed those previously stated initiation distinctions, the guru speaks enumeration for attainment of practiced knowledge.

[tal-a16-v185] The stated number, increased by forty, should be divided by seventy, and one should calculate initiation distinctions.

[tal-a16-v186] Here five lakhs, ninety-seven thousand, and eight hundred initiation distinctions are given in the Malini Tantra.

[tal-a16-v187] Seventy-fold and thirty-fold groups, purification, one principle and beyond, attendants, six rites, and duties yield four distinctions.

[tal-a16-v188] That knowledge composed of substance, free from birth and endowed with that, is thirty-five-fold from the union of enjoyment and liberation.

[tal-a16-v189] Enjoyment is thirty-two-fold by auspicious, pure, impure, and time distinctions; liberation is threefold; duty distinctions are seventy.

[tal-a16-v190] Initiation is divided in many ways by distinctions of purifier and purified; without the purified, it is seventy-fold.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sadya+utkrāntitastraidhaṃ sā cāsannamṛtau guroḥ / kāryetyājñā maheśasya śrīmadgahvarabhāṣitā dṛṣṭvā śiṣyaṃ jarāgrastaṃ vyādhinā paripīḍitam / utkramayya tatastvenaṃ paratattve niyojayet pañcatriṃśadamī bhedā gurorvā guruśiṣyayoḥ / uktadvaividhyakalanātsaptatiḥ parikīrtitāḥ etairbhedaiḥ puroktāṃstānbhedāndīkṣāgatānguruḥ / hatvā vadetprasaṃkhyānaṃ svabhyastajñānasiddhaye pañcāśītiśatī yā catvāriṃśatsamuttarā kathitā / tāṃ saptatyā bhittvā dīkṣābhedānsvayaṃ kalayet pañcakamiha lakṣāṇāṃ ca saptanavatiḥ sahasraparisaṃkhyā / aṣṭau śatāni dīkṣābhedo@yaṃ mālinītantre saptatidhā śoddhṛgaṇastriṃśaddhā śodhya ekatattvādiḥ / sāṇḍaḥ ṣaḍadhvarūpastathetikartavyatā caturbhedā dravyajñānamayī sā jananādivivarjitātha tadyuktā / pañcatriṃśaddhā punareṣā bhogāpavargasandhānāt yasmāddvātriṃśaddhā bhogaḥ śubhaśuddhyaśuddhikālabhidā / mokṣastredhā dviguṇā saptatiritikāryatābhedāḥ śodhanaśodhyavibhedāditikartavyatvabhedataścaiṣā / dīkṣā bahudhā bhinnā śodhyavihīnā tu saptatidhā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v191] From collecting mantra limb distinctions and enumerating fifteen distinctions of the purified and principles, the count arises.

[tal-a16-v192] The distinctions cannot be fully enumerated; unmixed distinctions exist, while mixed ones are many-fold.

[tal-a16-v193] Because purifier and purified distinctions exist, much remains to be done in enjoyment and accomplishment by the wise one's support.

[tal-a16-v194] Greater cause for greater fruit is no wonder; in liberation distinction remains through firm latent habit.

[tal-a16-v195] Even a small action is worthy of refuge; the teacher says again, when wealth, place, time and so on are present, or in knowledge alone.

[tal-a16-v196] Even in liberation, a broad collection of action and knowledge must be done, because consciousness fluctuation is varied and unsteady, joined gradually.

[tal-a16-v197] In each thing, shiva-natured establishment necessarily occurs; this truth, extracted by me, is for the disciple.

[tal-a16-v198] Thus in gradual awareness even a fool becomes shiva-natured, seeing the fortunate teacher who bestows such gradual shiva grace.

[tal-a16-v199] Even a child approaches shiva state by nondifference view and devotion strength; although discriminating activity remains, initiation gives liberation at the body's end.

[tal-a16-v200] Scripture declares that although the lord speaks thus, firm latent impression remains joined; even in liberation distinction exists, born of small or great action, such as same-world status.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-mantrāṇāṃ sakaletarasāṅganiraṅgādibhedasaṃkalanāt / śyodhyasya ca tattvādeḥ pañcadaśādyuktabhedaparigaṇanāt bhedānāṃ parigaṇanā na śakyate kartumityasaṃkīrṇāḥ / bhedāḥ saṃkīrṇāḥ punaranye bhūyastvakāriṇo bahudhā śodhakaśodhyādīnāṃ dvitrādivibhedasadbhāvāt / bhoge sādhye yadyadbahu kartavyaṃ tadāśrayenmatimān kāraṇabhūyastvaṃ kila phalabhūyastvāya kiṃ citram / apavarge natu bhedastenāsminvāsanādṛḍhatvajuṣā alpāpyāśrayaṇīyā kriyātha vijñānamātre vā / abhinavaguptaguruḥ punarāha hi sati vittadeśakālādau apavarge@pi hi vistīrṇakarmavijñānasaṃgrahaḥ kāryaḥ / cidvṛttervaicitryāccāñcalye@pi krameṇa sandhānāt tasmiṃstasminvastuni rūḍhiravaśyaṃ śivātmikā bhavati / tattvamidametadātmakametasmātproddhṛto mayā śiṣyaḥ itthaṃ kramasaṃvittau mūḍho@pi śivātmako bhavati / kramikatathāvidhaśivatānugrahasubhagaṃ ca daiśikaṃ paśyan śiśurapi tadabhedadṛśā bhaktibalāccābhyupaiti śivabhāvam / yadyapi vikalpavṛtterapi mokṣaṃ dīkṣayaiva dehānte śāstre provāca vibhustathāpi dṛḍhavāsanā yuktā / mokṣe@pyasti viśeṣaḥ kriyālpabhūyastvajaḥ salokādiḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v201] Thus some call that unfit; varied enjoyment only would be said, during the middle of life with residual impressions, with vow lapse and so on.

[tal-a16-v202] No obstacle net comes, because action abundance is not an obstacle for the liberation seeker; the person purified by seeded initiation is protected even in vow lapse and so on.

[tal-a16-v203] Liberation after enjoyment is not thus in seedless initiation; some think this fit, and scripture remembers that.

[tal-a16-v204] From transgressing the vow, O goddess, one becomes carnivorous for a hundred years.

[tal-a16-v205] Therefore, for a dull student, sequential action beginning with extraction of principles is fitting and extensive even for liberation, when it is capable of bestowing established Shiva-bhava.

[tal-a16-v206] But a guru always habituated in knowledge through meditation may, for the disciple's liberation, practice any means he wishes.

[tal-a16-v207] Thus, in the disciple's body, the path to be purified is placed as desired, and the purifying mantra is placed above according to the principles.

[tal-a16-v208] By the establishment of the two matrikas, the letter sequence told before is so placed for the purification of each principle.

[tal-a16-v209] Although the letter path is declared and to be purified, it is bound and maya-born; the purifier is another, Shiva-natured and supreme speech.

[tal-a16-v210] Sadyojyotis said in the commentary on Svayambhuva: indeed one sound is bound-natured, and another is Shiva-natured.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-iti kecittadayuktaṃ sa vicitro bhoga eva kathitaḥ syāt / saṃskāraśeṣavartanajīvitamadhye@sya samayalopādyam nāyāti vighnajālaṃ kriyābahutvaṃ mumukṣostat / yasmāt sabījadīkṣāsaṃskṛtapuruṣasya samayalopādye bhukte bhogānmokṣo naivaṃ nirbījadīkṣāyām / iti kecinmanyante yuktaṃ taccāpi yatsmṛtaṃ śāstre samayollaṅghanāddevi kravyādatvaṃ śataṃ samāḥ tasmāduruśiṣyamatau śivabhāvanirūḍhivitaraṇasamartham / kramikaṃ tattvoddharaṇādi karma mokṣe@pi yuktamativitatam yastu sadā bhāvanayā svabhyastajñānavānguruḥ sa śiśoḥ / apavargāya yathecchaṃ yaṃ kaṃcidupāyamanutiṣṭhet evaṃ śiṣyatanau śodhyaṃ nyasyādhvānaṃ yathepsitam / śodhakaṃ mantramupari nyasyettattvānusārataḥ dvayormātṛkayostattvasthityā varṇakramaḥ purā / kathitastaṃ tathā nyasyettattattattvaviśuddhaye varṇādhvā yadyapi proktaḥ śodhyaḥ pāśātmakastu saḥ / māyīyaḥ śodhakastvanyaḥ śivātmā paravāṅmayaḥ uvāca sadyojyotiśca vṛttau svāyambhuvasya tat / bāḍhameko hi pāśātmā śabdo@nyaśca śivātmakaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v211] Therefore the fitting purifier-purified relation of that very letter is also said in the previous scripture; they embrace it thus.

[tal-a16-v212] Having placed the faces beginning with Sadyojata and the limbs beginning with heart, five each, six times, one should perform the thirty-six placement from earth.

[tal-a16-v213] By reversal of the higher and lower in earth, three steps arise; then from water to ego through the support of five and eight.

[tal-a16-v214] Five steps are in the three named principles of intellect, root, and male color; three and one are in the two impure times; and one is in the controller.

[tal-a16-v215] One step is said here in kala and maya; in order, five steps are in vidyesvara, sadashiva, and shiva.

[tal-a16-v216] Nineteen steps should be the higher-lower arrangement, with halves, ones, twos, and the moon-eye pair.

[tal-a16-v217] The verse gives numerical counts of letters in the goddess's padas.

[tal-a16-v218] The verse defines letter counts ending at root and maya.

[tal-a16-v219] The verse states a rule and calls a vowel in the described placement.

[tal-a16-v220] The verse describes supreme placement in the shiva principle context.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tasmāttasyaiva varṇasya yuktā śodhakaśodhyatā / śrīpūrvaśāstre cāpyuktaṃ te tairāliṅgitā iti sadyojātādivaktrāṇi hṛdādyaṅgāni pañca ca / ṣaṭkṛtvo nyasya ṣaṭtriṃśannyāsaṃ kuryāddharāditaḥ parāparāyā vailomyāddharāyāṃ syātpadatrayam / tato jalādahaṅkāre pañcāṣṭakasamāśrayāt padāni pañca dhīmūlapuṃrāgākhye traye trayam / ekaṃ tvaśuddhavitkāladvaye caikaṃ niyāmake kalāmāyādvaye caikaṃ padamuktamiha kramāt / vidyeśvarasadāśaktiśiveṣu padapañcakam ekonaviṃśatiḥ seyaṃ padānāṃ syātparāparā / sārdhaṃ caikaṃ caikaṃ sārdhaṃ dve dve śaśī dṛgatha yugmam trāṇi dṛgabdhiścandraḥ śrutiḥ śaśī pañca vidhumahaścandrāḥ / ekānnaviṃśatau syādakṣarasaṃkhyā padeṣviyaṃ devyāḥ haldvayayutavasucitraguparisaṃkhyātasvavarṇāyāḥ / mūlāntaṃ sārdhavarṇaṃ syānmāyāntaṃ varṇamekakam śaktyantamekamaparānyāse vidhirudīritaḥ / māyāntaṃ haltataḥ śaktiparyante svara ucyate niṣkale śivatattve vai paro nyāsaḥ paroditaḥ / parāparāpadānyeva hyaghoryādyaṣṭakadvaye

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v221] The verse instructs placing mantras in principles according to letter counts.

[tal-a16-v222] The verse arranges remainders and seeds across all principles.

[tal-a16-v223] The verse records that others accepted seed-like placement for clusters.

[tal-a16-v224] The verse says purifying placement purifies all purifiable.

[tal-a16-v225] The verse says element purification arises by placement alone.

[tal-a16-v226] The verse questions why a stated thing is not taken elsewhere.

[tal-a16-v227] The verse identifies a formerly declared placement.

[tal-a16-v228] The verse gives a count involving ear padas.

[tal-a16-v229] In the placement of the pure purifying mantra, by the goddess's glory, eighteen fingers measure one foot, while another foot has another measure.

[tal-a16-v230] From the fourth foot in the six-foot context, two measures called supreme and inferior are twelve and twelve, with another as before above the principles.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-mantrāstadanusāreṇa tattveṣvetaddvayaṃ kṣipet / piṇḍākṣarāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ varṇasaṃkhyā vibhedataḥ avyaktāntaṃ svare nyasyā śeṣaṃ śeṣeṣu yojayet / bījāni sarvatattveṣu vyāptṛtvena prakalpayet piṇḍānāṃ bījavannyāsamanye tu pratipedire / akṛte vātha śodhyasya nyāse vastubalāt sthiteḥ śodhakanyāsamātreṇa sarvaṃ śodhyaṃ viśudhyati / śrīmanmṛtyuñjayādau ca kathitaṃ parameṣṭhinā adhunā nyāsamātreṇa bhūtaśuddhiḥ prajāyate / dehaśuddhyarthamapyetattulyametena vastutaḥ anyaprakaraṇoktaṃ yadyuktaṃ prakaraṇāntare / jñāpakatvena sākṣādvā tatkiṃ nānyatra gṛhyate mālinīmātṛkāṅgasya nyāso yo@rcāvidhau purā / proktaḥ kevalasaṃśoddhṛmantranyāse sa eva tu tripadī dvayordvayoḥ syātpratyekamathāṣṭasu śrutipadāni / dikcandracandrarasaraviśaraśaradṛgdṛṅmṛgāṅkaśaśigaṇane aṅgulamāne devyā aṣṭādaśa vaibhavena padamanyat / aparaṃ mānamidaṃ syāt kevalaśodhakamanunyāse turyapadātpadaṣaṭke mānadvitayaṃ parāparaparākhyam / dvādaśakaṃ dvādaśakaṃ tattvopari pūrvavattvanyat

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v231] According to the intent of pure purifying mantra placement, the great god again declares a placement opposite to that principle-order placement.

[tal-a16-v232] In the partless, the foot is one syllable up to three in the earthly context; by such and so on, the principle-gone order placement is declared.

[tal-a16-v233] Again in the Mālinī Tantra, from the distinction of class and knowledge, the lord says the feet are in two ways and describes another kind of named placement.

[tal-a16-v234] Each is to be known as two fingers; there the first three feet are eight fingers, four, ten fingers thence beyond.

[tal-a16-v235] In two fingers there are two feet and other; six fingers thence beyond; and twelve fingers other, two in five fingers separate.

[tal-a16-v236] Two feet are four-jointed, and other two are two-jointed; thus the independent placement of the supreme-inferior goddess is called.

[tal-a16-v237] To show that the two knowledges are joined in the disciple's body by pervader-ness only, no separate placement was formed.

[tal-a16-v238] Thus in the placement of the purifying mantra, from its ray union the noose-net would dissolve, from the meditation power of the teacher.

[tal-a16-v239] In the principle to be purified, for all sources at the same time, from birth and enjoyment, at the destruction of action there would be liberation.

[tal-a16-v240] Wonderful with so many bodies of the atom, even for the enjoyer, the mind-connection is not clear, having universe union and separation.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kevalaśodhakamantranyāsābhiprāyato mahādevaḥ / tattvakramoditamapi nyāsaṃ punarāha tadviruddhamapi niṣkale padamekārṇaṃ yāvattrīṇi tu pārthive / ityādinā tattvagatakramanyāsa udīritaḥ punaśca mālinītantre vargavidyāvibhedataḥ / dvidhā padānītyuktvākhyannyāsamanyādṛśaṃ vibhuḥ ekaikaṃ dvyaṅgulaṃ jñeyaṃ tatra pūrvaṃ padatrayam / aṣṭāṅgulāni catvāri daśāṅgulamataḥ param dvyaṅgule dve pade cānye ṣaḍaṅgulamataḥ param / dvādaśāṅgulamanyacca dve@nye pañcāṅgule pṛthak padadvayaṃ catuṣparva tathānye dve dviparvaṇī / evaṃ parāparādevyāḥ svatantro nyāsa ucyate vidyādvayaṃ śiṣyatanau vyāptṛtvenaiva yojayet / iti darśayituṃ nāsya pṛthaṅnyāsaṃ nyarūpayat evaṃ śodhakamantrasya nyāse tadraśmiyogataḥ / pāśajālaṃ vilīyeta taddhyānabalato guroḥ śodhyatattve samastānāṃ yonīnāṃ tulyakālataḥ / jananādbhogataḥ karmakṣaye syādapavṛktatā dehaistāvadbhirasyāṇościtraṃ bhokturapi sphuṭam / mano@nusandhirno viśvasaṃyogapravibhāgavat

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v241] By necessity, the mind's activity is only in the body; beyond that there is no continuity, because it is constructed through one mind and united senses.

[tal-a16-v242] Local activity and knowledge of the self occur there; that object-knowledge does not deserve continuity in other bodies.

[tal-a16-v243] When that mind's body activity certainly becomes pure through yoga, mantra, and rite, then the knower acts.

[tal-a16-v244] As pure mind sees quickly even when far, so in initiation of understanding there is seeing of those worlds.

[tal-a16-v245] When one wishes initiation free from birth and so on, then the plan 'I lift from this' is proper deliberation.

[tal-a16-v246] Even without purification, the purifier rite there by mantra performs the birth sequence free from element union.

[tal-a16-v247] In the single purifier rite excluding birth and so on, only that purifier container should be imagined.

[tal-a16-v248] In initiation by substance union, sesame, ghee, unbroken rice, and grains are offered by respective mantra for birth union and separation.

[tal-a16-v249] When knowledge initiation is done to the disciple, then intensely by that mantra speech force one sees from the non-conceptual.

[tal-a16-v250] Concept is indeed speech-composed; that reflective one is mantra-self, and reflection is pure and bondage-natured.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-niyatyā manaso dehamātre vṛttistataḥ param / nānusandhā yataḥ saikasvāntayuktākṣakalpitā pradeśavṛtti ca jñānamātmanastatra tatra tat / bhogyajñānaṃ nānyadeheṣvanusandhānamarhati yadā tu manasastasya dehavṛtterapi dhruvam / yogamantrakriyādeḥ syādvaimalyaṃ tadvidā tadā yathāmalaṃ mano dūrasthitamapyāśu paśyati / tathā pratyayadīkṣāyāṃ tattadbhuvanadarśanam jananādiviyuktāṃ tu yadā dīkṣāṃ cikīrṣati / tadāsmāduddharāmīti yuktamūhaprakalpanam yadā śodhyaṃ vinā śoddhṛnyāsastatrāpi mantrataḥ / jananādikramaṃ kuryāttattvasaṃśleṣavarjitam ekākiśoddhṛnyāse ca jananādivivarjane / tacchoddhṛsaṃpuṭaṃ nāma kevalaṃ parikalpayet dravyayogena dīkṣāyāṃ tilājyākṣatataṇḍulam / tattanmantreṇa juhuyājjanmayogaviyogayoḥ yadā vijñānadīkṣāṃ tu kuryācchiṣyaṃ tadā bhṛśam / tanmantrasaṃjalpabalāt paśyedā cāvikalpakāt vikalpaḥ kila saṃjalpamayo yatsa vimarśakaḥ / mantrātmāsau vimarśaśca śuddho@pāśavatātmakaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v251] Because eternal beginningless boon shiva identity is constructed, by its union the teacher's concept may attain shivahood.

[tal-a16-v252] In shri sara shastra this is spoken by the supreme lord: comprehension of meaning is object-subject-formed.

[tal-a16-v253] That very mantra-power, spread out in the mantra continuum, is declared as mantra-power of reflection-nature.

[tal-a16-v254] Reflection is twofold and divides mantras by purity and impurity; this is said in the holy Pauṣkara, and Brahma, Vishnu, and others are egg-born.

[tal-a16-v255] The primary attached beings are sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic; through their impure reflection the teacher becomes absorbed in that.

[tal-a16-v256] Vaishnava and others are declared bound souls, not fit for the lord's rule; mantras standing on the pure path, such as Shiva-bhattaraka and others, are fit.

[tal-a16-v257] The teacher seen by holy Matanga and others is absorbed in that and is Shiva; but can independent speech union alone produce reflection?

[tal-a16-v258] From where before? If from reflection, from where? In determination, the first would give unwaveringness from the teacher.

[tal-a16-v259] If there is transmitted speech, it too comes from another teacher; in previous order, before, it is from the first teacher.

[tal-a16-v260] Speech is indeed transmitted and exists today also; let it be grasped, even if such speech by force is independent.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-nityaścānādivaradaśivābhedopakalpitaḥ / tadyogāddaiśikasyāpi vikalpaḥ śivatāṃ vrajet śrīsāraśāstre tadidaṃ parameśena bhāṣitam / arthasya pratipattiryā grāhyagrāhakarūpiṇī sā eva mantraśaktistu vitatā mantrasantatau / parāmarśasvabhāvetthaṃ mantraśaktirudāhṛtā parāmarśo dvidhā śuddhāśuddhatvānmantrabhedakaḥ / uktaṃ śrīpauṣkare@nye ca brahmaviṣṇvādayo@ṇḍagāḥ prādhānikāḥ sāñjanāste sāttvarājasatāmasāḥ / tairaśuddhaparāmarśāttanmayībhāvito guruḥ vaiṣṇavādiḥ paśuḥ prokto na yogyaḥ patiśāsane / ye mantrāḥ śuddhamārgasthāḥ śivabhaṭṭārakādayaḥ śrīmanmataṅgādidṛśā tanmayo hi guruḥ śivaḥ / nanu svatantrasaṃjalpayogādastu vimarśitā prākkutaḥ sa vimarśāccetkutaḥ so@pi nirūpaṇe / ādyastathāvikalpatvapradaḥ syādupadeṣṭṛtaḥ yaḥ saṃkrānto@bhijalpaḥ syāttasyāpyanyopadeṣṭṛtaḥ / pūrvapūrvakramāditthaṃ ya evādiguroḥ purā saṃjalpo hyabhisaṃkrāntaḥ so@dyāpyastīti gṛhyatām / yastathāvidhasaṃjalpabalātko@pi svatantrakaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v261] Reflection is imagined; that too is indeed that self, well-determined, like pot and jar; or if difference is determined, thus.

[tal-a16-v262] That also gives other imagination and is not to be regarded; with effort it is valued, as doing thus, clearly in the fitting of imagination.

[tal-a16-v263] Hand and transmitted speech, those two, how indeed are they mixed from word to another word? By that, learning is interrupted.

[tal-a16-v264] But from practice, that directly reflects wonderful narrative; its reflection rises, and ancient own reflection may shine.

[tal-a16-v265] Natural awareness sets the limit for conceptualization arising from mantra meaning.

[tal-a16-v266] Mantra is honored when difference is seen through prior knowledge forms.

[tal-a16-v267] Another concept is unnecessary because the mark belongs to that alone.

[tal-a16-v268] The mantra-tantra expert states the mark for awakening mantra meaning.

[tal-a16-v269] In absence of a mantra-meaning knower, the guru practices mantra identification.

[tal-a16-v270] One should make a guru when practice produces equal speech through meditation.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-vimarśaḥ kalpyate so@pi tadātmaiva suniścitaḥ / ghaṭakumbha itītthaṃ vā yadi bhedo nirūpyate so@pyanyakalpanādāyī hyanādṛtyaḥ prayatnataḥ / paṇāyate karotīti vikalpasyocitau sphuṭam karapāṇyabhijalpau tau saṃkīryetāṃ kathaṃ kila / śabdācchabdāntare tena vyutpattirvyavadhānataḥ vyavahārāttu sā sākṣāccitropākhyāvimarśinī / tadvimarśodayaḥ prācyasvavimarśamayaḥ sphuret yāvadbālasya saṃvittirakṛtrimavimarśane / tena tanmantraśabdārthaviśeṣotthaṃ vikalpanam śabdāntarotthādbhedena paśyatā mantra ādṛtaḥ / yaccāpi bījapiṇḍāderuktaṃ prāgbodharūpakam tattasyaiva kuto@nyasya tatkasmādanyakalpanā / etadarthaṃ guroryatnāllakṣaṇe tatra tatra tat lakṣaṇaṃ kathitaṃ hyeṣa mantratantraviśāradaḥ / tena mantrārthasaṃbodhe mantravārtikamādarāt ūhāpohaprayogaṃ vā sarvathā gururācaret / mantrārthavidabhāve tu sarvathā mantratanmayam guruṃ kuryāt tadabhyāsāttatsaṃkalpamayo hyasau / tatsamānābhisaṃjalpo yadā mantrārthabhāvanāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v271] In complete equality there is no difference; purpose action follows.

[tal-a16-v272] By reason, one sees the same purpose action even from other speech.

[tal-a16-v273] The truthful speaker is Shiva, and what he says becomes mantra.

[tal-a16-v274] This is not the position of Abhinavagupta, whose self is offered to mantra.

[tal-a16-v275] A mantra-offered mind removes poison, and that mantra word is supreme.

[tal-a16-v276] The beautiful lover, purified by that, is satisfied in himself.

[tal-a16-v277] Thus mantra-recitation-imbued, speaking even other things — unwilling too, of that form — he does the deed, certainly.

[tal-a16-v278] Imagining even one meaning — since he sees another too — poison-removing mantras and the rest, so said in the former Sri-teaching.

[tal-a16-v279] Or even in poison-destruction, diversity from cause-difference — from endless effect-differences like tissue-growth it will arise.

[tal-a16-v280] Thus from mantra-recitation-imagination-practice union — the to-be-meditated thing's clarity — from union with recitation-diminution.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-gurorbhavettadā sarvasāmye ko bheda ucyatām / aṃśenāpyatha vaiṣamye na tato@rthakriyā hi sā gomayātkīṭataḥ kīṭa ityevaṃ nyāyato yadā / saṃjalpāntarato@pyarthakriyāṃ tāmeva paśyati tadaiṣa satyasaṃjalpaḥ śiva eveti kathyate / sa yadvakti tadeva syānmantro bhogāpavargadaḥ naiṣo@bhinavaguptasya pakṣo mantrārpitātmanaḥ / yo@rthakriyāmāha bhinnāṃ kīṭayorapi tādṛśoḥ mantrārpitamanāḥ kiṃcidvadanyattu viṣaṃ haret / tanmantra eva śabdaḥ sa paraṃ tatra ghaṭādivat kāntāsaṃbhogasaṃjalpasundaraḥ kāmukaḥ sadā / tatsaṃskṛto@pyanyadeṣa kurvansvātmani tṛpyati tathā tanmantrasaṃjalpabhāvito@nyadapi bruvan / anicchurapi tadrūpastathā kāryakaro dhruvam vikalpayannapyekārthaṃ yato@nyadapi paśyati / viṣāpahārimantrādītyuktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāsane yadi vā viṣanāśe@pi hetubhedādvicitratā / dhātvāpyāyādikānantakāryabhedādbhaviṣyati tadevaṃ mantrasaṃjalpavikalpābhyāsayogataḥ / bhāvyavastusphuṭībhāvaḥ saṃjalpahrāsayogataḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v281] This one makes real the thing itself — not this chatter again; he takes manifestation-means — but once manifested, what use is that there?

[tal-a16-v282] Thus in chatter-decrease, very-clear-natured, unartificial-reflection-natured — the non-conceptual thing flashes.

[tal-a16-v283] And undifferentiated consciousness, just as it sees clearly — exactly so, by that selfhood even of the externally standing thing.

[tal-a16-v284] Especially for the maya-shiva-difference-holding, discussion is the liberation-means — bondage and liberation then indeed.

[tal-a16-v285] Even in doubt, of the teacher enjoying properly undivided Shiva-nature — expectation until the non-conceptual is not employed.

[tal-a16-v286] Of that-reflection-nature indeed is she, to be spoken as mantra-deity — near great consciousness, so said in Srigama teaching.

[tal-a16-v287] As the near-standing sufficiently accomplish success for kings and others, king-approaching, quickly — so mantras and the rest, the supreme.

[tal-a16-v288] Pregnant with stated intent, that is said in Srimalini-mata — of mantras the characteristic — when sages asked why, indeed.

[tal-a16-v289] They desire yoga-oneness of thing with thing — that thing is declared knowable, for establishing rejectability and the rest.

[tal-a16-v290] For that accomplishment, the knowledge spoken by Shiva as described — for seeded-yoga accomplishment, mantra-characteristics too suffice.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-vastveva bhāvayatyeṣa na saṃjalpamimaṃ punaḥ / gṛhṇāti bhāsanopāyaṃ bhāte tatra tu tena kim evaṃ saṃjalpanirhrāse suparisphuṭatātmakam / akṛttrimavimarśātma sphuredvastvavikalpakam nirvikalpā ca sā saṃvidyadyathā paśyati sphuṭam / tattathaiva tathātmatvādvastuno@pi bahiḥsthiteḥ viśeṣatastvamāyīyaśivatābhedaśālinaḥ / mokṣe@bhyupāyaḥ saṃjalpo bandhamokṣau tataḥ kila vikalpe@pi guroḥ samyagabhinnaśivatājuṣaḥ / avikalpakaparyantapratīkṣā nopayujyate tadvimarśasvabhāvā hi sā vācyā mantradevatā / mahāsaṃvitsamāsannetyuktaṃ śrīgamaśāsane nikaṭasthā yathā rājñāmanyeṣāṃ sādhayantyalam / siddhiṃ rājopagāṃ śīghramevaṃ mantrādayaḥ parām uktābhiprāyagarbhaṃ taduktaṃ śrīmālinīmate / mantrāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kasmādityukte munibhiḥ kila yogamekatvamicchanti vastuno@nyena vastunā / tadvastu jñeyamityuktaṃ heyatvādiprasiddhaye tatprasiddhyai śivenoktaṃ jñānaṃ yadupavarṇitam / sabījayogasaṃsiddhyai mantralakṣaṇamapyalam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v291] And no eligibility in Shaiva yoga without initiation — by action-knowledge distinction it is declared twofold.

[tal-a16-v292] Twofold it is to be done, as cited by him — and yoga-eligibility would not be by this one alone.

[tal-a16-v293] Also mantra-entitlement and liberation by Shiva-initiation — by this too it is declared — the yogin, for tattva-unity accomplishment.

[tal-a16-v294] Mantra alone as root refuge, honoring the non-conceptual end — by mantra-practice accomplishing enjoyment or even liberation.

[tal-a16-v295] For attaining eligibility there, take initiation from the teacher — by that, whatever mantra-knowledge-yoga power, accomplish.

[tal-a16-v296] That too — of the guru-yoked child in another tattva — initiation indeed applies to him; in consecration he is consecrated.

[tal-a16-v297] By own power alone the wise gains enjoyment or liberation — thereby through knowledge-yoga power, previously becoming a basic initiate.

[tal-a16-v298] The spiritual son would not be so great — but fitting to own strength; but who is deprived of knowledge-yoga is blind, as on a path.

[tal-a16-v299] Teacher-dependent indeed in enjoyment and liberation, in every way — and initiation alone, even without knowledge of one's own inner, releases indeed, so said.

[tal-a16-v300] Release indeed, so said by reasoning and scripture formerly — but the child considering only initiated connections, connection...
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-na cādhikāritā dīkṣāṃ vinā yoge@sti śāṅkare / kriyājñānavibhedena sā ca dvedhā nigadyate dvividhā sā prakartavyā tena caitadudāhṛtam / naca yogādhikāritvamekamevānayā bhavet api mantrādhikāritvaṃ muktiśca śivadīkṣayā / anenaitadapi proktaṃ yogī tattvaikyasiddhaye mantramevāśrayenmūlaṃ nirvikalpāntamādṛtaḥ / mantrābhyāsena bhogaṃ vā mokṣaṃ vāpi prasādhayan tatrādhikāritālabdhyai dīkṣāṃ gṛhṇīta daiśikāt / tena mantrajñānayogabalādyadyatprasādhayet tatsyādasyānyatattve@pi yuktasya guruṇā śiśoḥ / dīkṣā hyasyopayujyeta saṃskriyāyāṃ sa saṃskṛtaḥ svabalenaiva bhogaṃ vā mokṣaṃ vā labhate budhaḥ / tena vijñānayogādibalī prāk samayī bhavan putrako vā na tāvānsyādapitu svabalocitaḥ / yastu vijñānayogādivandhyaḥ so@ndho yathā pathi daiśikāyatta eva syādbhoge muktau ca sarvathā / dīkṣā ca kevalā jñānaṃ vināpi nijamāntaram mocikaiveti kathitaṃ yuktyā cāgamataḥ purā / yastu dīkṣākṛtāmevāpekṣya yojanikāṃ śiśuḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a16-v301] Knowledge becomes manifest in the fitting way; the yogin who takes refuge in yoga becomes united and attains identification with that reality.

[tal-a16-v302] Then all states depend on guru initiation, mantra, and scripture, especially for wicked beings among past, present, and future.

[tal-a16-v303] Purification of actions should be done; it is not for one desiring enjoyment, while good souls are distinguished from those seeking worldly pleasures like kingdom and heaven.

[tal-a16-v304] Having abandoned transcendent enjoyment, one desiring his enjoyment performs there a material initiation with ghee, sesame, and similar offerings, even in auspicious matters.

[tal-a16-v305] The best teacher should offer, saying 'I purify his action'; but in knowledge-filled initiation, that becomes pure by union.

[tal-a16-v306] By the force of the guru rooted in self-awareness, destruction occurs; when his inauspicious actions become pure, then auspiciousness follows.

[tal-a16-v307] By relying on one's own gradation in the path, this production arises, from the completion of enjoyment of fruits obtained by auspicious ripening sequence.

[tal-a16-v308] Where this one is placed and stands, when future action is destroyed, it concerns future beings differing between the first body and another body.

[tal-a16-v309] When the inauspicious part is purified, there is no decrease of enjoyment itself; this enjoyer constantly enjoys from the abode of maya to the end.

[tal-a16-v310] Nothing gives painful fruit even in the path beginning with the body; then in the abode of maya all pleasant enjoyments are enjoyed.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sphuṭībhūtyai taducitaṃ jñānaṃ yogamathāśritaḥ / so@pi yatraiva yuktaḥ syāttanmayatvaṃ prapadyate gurudīkṣāmantraśāstrādhīnasarvasthitistataḥ / duṣṭānāmeva sarveṣāṃ bhūtabhavyabhaviṣyatām karmaṇāṃ śodhanaṃ kāryaṃ bubhukṣorna śubhātmanām / yaḥ punarlaukikaṃ bhogaṃ rājyasvargādikaṃ śiśuḥ tyaktvā lokottaraṃ bhogamīpsustasya śubheṣvapi / tatra dravyamayīṃ dīkṣāṃ kurvannājyatilādikaiḥ karmāsya śodhayāmīti juhuyāddaiśikottamaḥ / jñānamayyāṃ tu dīkṣāyāṃ tadviśuddhyati sandhitaḥ guroḥ svasaṃvidrūḍhasya balāttatprakṣayo bhavet / yadāsyāśubhakarmāṇi śuddhāni syustadā śubham svatāratamyāśrayaṇādadhvamadhye prasūtidam / śubhapākakramopāttaphalabhogasamāptitaḥ yatraiṣa yojitastatstho bhāvikarmakṣaye kṛte / bhāvināṃ cādyadehasthadehāntaravibhedinām aśubhāṃśaviśuddhau syādbhogasyaivānupakṣayaḥ / bhuñjānasyāsya satataṃ bhogānmāyālayāntataḥ na duḥkhaphaladaṃ dehādyadhvamadhye@pi kiṃcana / tato māyālaye bhuktasamastasukhabhogakaḥ

chunks.l2: [tal-a16-v311] Dissolution goes in the partless and in the with-parts by the force of union; thus this knowable was told at the time of initiation, as from the guru.
